A2-210 corrects three things the service said about itself that were untrue. (1) A provider timeout was reported as `network_error` on the API lane, because `AbortSignal.timeout()` aborts with a DOMException named 'TimeoutError' and the code tested for 'AbortError'; and as `execution_error` on the CLI lane, because `child_process.spawn`'s `timeout` option emits `close`, not an ETIMEDOUT `error`, so the catch block was never entered at all. Both measured on this host, Node v24.20.0, against a local non-answering HTTP server and a local `sleep` — no production service was contacted. This had silently disabled A2-207/#139's rule that a caller's own shorter budget must not feed the shared per-model breaker: it keys on errorType === 'timeout', which neither lane could ever emit. #139's tests passed because they rejected with a hand-built DOMException named 'AbortError'; that fake is corrected here and is red at base. (2) `CircuitBreaker.getState()` returned the stored state while `open -> half_open` happened only inside `check()`, so an idle model read `open` for as long as it got no traffic — measured live by A2-206 on `deepseek-flash`, nextRetryAt 997 s in the past, next real request successful first try. (3) `getCapabilities().maxTimeout` was advertised to callers in the catalog and read by no code path; it is now the per-connector ceiling, which is a behaviour change for a caller who asks for more time than a connector advertises. Merging this PR redeploys production MC, so it is left open for the control session.
